mutations.because: the confinement check is skipped: a ref `resolveAssetPath` refuses is handed to the parser as though it had passed. `/etc/passwd` then parses to no campaign and answers ENOENT rather than undefined, and `../outside.png` parses the same way — so a run over a brief naming a path outside the assets tree fails loudly where fs skipped the asset cleanly, and a brief naming `/etc/passwd` gets an error naming an asset rather than being ignored. The confinement decision is the ONE thing this port must not make twice: it is made once, in `resolveAssetPath`, so the object port's refusals and `FileSystemInputAssets`' cannot drift apart.

a failed read stays in the memo as a rejected promise, and every later read of that ref joins it and is handed the same failure forever. The run that dies is the one waiting on an upload: the preview that ran before it, the re-run after it, and every retry in between all report a missing logo while the store has held the right bytes the whole time — and a rejected promise has no timeout, so nothing would ever clear it. Forgetting only the failures IS the memo's contract; a cache that remembers a refusal is a cache that lies. The retry test is the only case that can see it (a MISSING ref, then the object arriving, then the read), because every other test reads once.
command: the next read retries the store and finds the new object
